svg.title: Hohmann transfer: low Earth orbit to geostationary orbit
svg.desc: Animated Hohmann transfer from a 300 km low Earth orbit (LEO) to geostationary orbit (GEO). Orbit radii and Earth are drawn to the true scale (r₁ = 6,678 km, r₂ = 42,164 km, ratio 6.31; Earth 6,371 km). μ = 398,600.4418 km³/s². Circular LEO speed √(μ/r₁) = 7.726 km/s; transfer ellipse a = 24,421 km, e = 0.7265; perigee speed 10.152 km/s so Δv₁ = 2.426 km/s; apogee speed 1.608 km/s, GEO speed 3.075 km/s so Δv₂ = 1.467 km/s; total 3.893 km/s. Transfer time π√(a³/μ) = 18,990 s = 5.28 h. LEO period 90.5 min, GEO period 23.93 h. The craft's position on the ellipse is sampled at equal time steps from Kepler's equation M = E − e·sin E, so it visibly slows towards apogee; 1 s of animation = 45 min. Source: docs/EQUATIONS.md §1.9 (result 3.893 km/s = 2.43 + 1.47 km/s, 5.3 h coast). Plane change ignored.
svg.text: Two burns from low orbit to geostationary

g.text: half an ellipse; Kepler slows it to 1.61 km/s

svg.text: Radii to scale: 6,678 km vs 42,164 km (×6.31). Timing is Kepler-true; 1 s of animation ≈ 45 min.
